A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniSpatial and provide readable main text and appendices. Rendered figures, tables, equations and image-only examples support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original model and human evaluations, PointGraph and SpatialCoT experiments, training and transfer results, and appendix analyses of evaluation strategies and annotator agreement.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds joint-component evaluations, depth/orientation analyses, model standard deviations and additional SpatialCoT results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a combined inference variant using PointGraph scene-graph cues together with SpatialCoT novel views; v2 evaluated the augmentations separately. Their individual procedures in Section 3.3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The datasets, four-category/50-subtask OmniSpatial coverage and external benchmark coverage are retained. New analyses reuse existing tasks and images. Applying SpatialCoT to the already evaluated Complex-Logic track does not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 12 introduces Manual CoT as the comparator in a SpatialCoT experiment on Complex-Logic; v2's SpatialCoT comparison in Table 4 used Zero-shot CoT. The main benchmark comparator roster is unchanged. Table 12's heading 'GPT-2.5-Flash-Thinking' leaves that model's identity ambiguous.

E3.justification: Section 3.2.1 changes the reported allocation of SpatialViz, PhysBench, ViewSpatial and DrivingVQA samples from the test set to the training set, retaining the 6.9K/1.5K split sizes. This establishes a reported setting revision, not a rerun. Appendix F adds joint-component controls, depth/orientation binning and coarse-category aggregation.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained prompting and evaluation-format ablations, Appendix F adds a joint-component ablation and quantitative error analyses stratified by object depth and orientation. These substantially expand testing of component complementarity and failure conditions. The four illustrated failure cases already appeared in v2 Figure 1; their redisplay is not new case evidence.

E5.justification: v2 already reports five-run model averages and bootstrap confidence intervals for human accuracy. v3 Table 11 newly supplies standard deviations for overall and coarse-category model scores across the main comparison. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Table 10 retains SpatialCoT averages of 47.58 and 42.90 for GPT-4.1-mini and Qwen-VL2.5-3B, adding joint-variant scores of 48.70 and 43.75. Complex-Logic and depth/orientation results are also added. Table 9 changes overall human accuracy reporting from 92.6±1.5 to 92.6±2.5. Existing Tables 2–8 retain their results.

T1.justification: Section 2's formal visual-spatial mapping and taxonomy are retained. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are added or revised; the new appendix contains empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions, large human–model performance gap, and claims about PointGraph and SpatialCoT. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2 substantially expands mechanism-oriented discussion of existing failures, proposing route visualizations for imagined-pose planning, enhanced temporal memory for action sequences, and generative intermediate states for paper folding. These are presented as hypotheses or future remedies. The earlier limitations remain intact in Appendix G.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Metric3D v2 and SoFar as tools for the new depth/orientation analysis, newly mentions iterative system-prompt tuning, and states that source code is supplied in supplementary materials. The actual prompt templates and project, code and dataset links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds GS-Reasoner and Metric3D citations and removes citations to AHA, RT-2 and Wake et al.'s robotics work. GS-Reasoner's grounded spatial reasoning receives a brief description, and Appendix E adds a strongest-to-date comprehensiveness assertion. The added published Wang et al. entry duplicates a work already cited in v2.

P1.justification: Most original prose and organization are preserved. Spatial VLM related work moves from Appendix B.1 to Section 5.2, with localized edits. v3 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, Appendix F, conference headers and another corresponding-author designation.

P2.justification: The appendix gains Tables 10–12, a depth/orientation diagram with bar charts, and four enlarged failure panels extracted from Figure 1. This substantially expands the visual presentation, including an aggregate uncertainty table. Existing main figures remain, while prompt and sample figures are preserved as Figures 13–18.

improvement.justification: The joint-component experiment, depth/orientation diagnostics and model standard deviations provide a limited net gain in diagnostic coverage and transparency while preserving the main empirical evidence. Reporting problems constrain the benefit: Table 12's Qwen average of 29.27 exceeds both subtask scores, 29.01 and 28.52, and Table 11's standard-deviation framing is not reconciled with Appendix C.3's bootstrap-confidence-interval description of human uncertainty.
